chapter: WWL and the Roosevelt Fountain Lounge
title: The band room and Sandy's escapades
summary: Frank describes playing double headers and the band room 256, and tells stories of cellist Sandy.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Yeah, well, they used to open it up on Saturday night at nighttime. They used to go all the way over to Barone Street. So I played double headers in there. I played the lunch with Albert Corson. I worked with about a half a dozen bands at nighttime. And I stayed in the hotel. I just didn't have to worry about anything. You stayed in a room in the hotel?
No. No, no, no, no. No, no. I stayed in the hotel. But we had a room, 256. Remember, Godfrey?

Yeah, the band room, yeah. And Sandy used to bring his gals up in there. And he was over there. And Gordon told me, he says, I caught him with his head and I dress up. And he says, I can't say anything more than that. But he says, I caught him. And Sandy says, what were you doing? He said, ha, ha, ha, ha, ha.
You know how Sandy laughed at all? That's when Sandy was giving him. I'm telling you, he was something. You mean the United States or Mexico?

One of his illegitimate children were born. The dentist. It was a dentist's dog. And the dentist came around the hotel and was going to kill him. He had a gun. He was going to kill him. And he says, oh, I did the right thing. He said, I paid the hospital bill. He says, I did the right thing. I paid the hospital bill.
I thought we were at the Sangin Theater. He had some gal over there that comes in there sitting in the front row with the little baby. And he's dying up there. He's planning an overture.
That Mexican, I'm telling you. He was something else. He sure was.
